observations: The trusted transition receipt marks imports + content-hash as changed, so only dependency and duplicate-content bodies are stale by truth.
Scoped truth retains the still-valid expensive search body across canonical transitions, producing four additional cache hits.

Scoped truth produces more budget-eviction bytes than full invalidation in this trace because valid expensive state survives long enough to compete for scarce cache space; this is expected and is kept as evidence, not treated as a failure.
After stale bodies are removed, the value-aware budget policy may evict still-valid lower-value bodies to enforce the hard 900 KB ceiling.
Unreceipted canonical state changes still fall back to complete budget-cache invalidation.
A transition receipt bound to the wrong canonical base is rejected before cache mutation.
timingBoundary: Upstream transition-receipt generation and direct-baseline verification are excluded. Measured time includes stale invalidation/fallback, hard-budget eviction, materialization, and post-transition execution.
strongestSupportedClaim: In this deterministic workspace harness, truth-scoped invalidation and hard-budget retention can operate in one lifecycle: stale derived bodies are removed from trusted hash-bound transition evidence first, still-valid bodies remain eligible for retention, and only then does deterministic budget eviction choose among valid bodies. This preserved exact direct-baseline outputs while substantially reducing rematerialization in the measured transition trace.
boundaries: Does not prove universal speedup or production-scale superiority.
Does not prove globally optimal retention or eviction.
Does not prove automatic arbitrary dependency inference.
Scoped correctness depends on complete and truthful upstream changed-domain evidence.
Transition-receipt generation is not free and is outside this benchmark timing.
Single hosted timing samples are observational, not a statistical performance distribution.
Does not create RAM, compute cycles, energy, or free resources.
nextGate: Move from full-state body identity toward versioned domain/body identities so trusted unchanged domains can survive more granular canonical updates without hashing or treating the whole state as one monolith; then test repeated samples and multi-capability/dependency-aware budget execution.
